MCSC-101.alt: Comparison of greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, backtracking and branch-and-bound
MCSC-101.note: The Fibonacci dependency tree is illustrative but not correct: F(4) depends on F(3) and F(2), not two F(3) nodes. The greedy tree is not a worked fractional-knapsack calculation.

MCSC-102.alt: Bayes theorem with a probability tree and a numerical example
Sampling, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing illustrated as an inference map
MCSC-102.note: The shaded area beyond a critical value represents a rejection region; a p-value is calculated from the observed test statistic, not necessarily from that critical value.

MCSC-103.alt: Five network layers on a sender and receiver with encapsulation and decapsulation
MCSC-103.note: At the receiver, processing proceeds upward from the physical layer to the application layer; some arrows in the illustration point downwards. Real packets encapsulate the transport header inside the network payload.

MCSC-103.alt: Network management and security diagram showing SNMP, authentication and backup
MCSC-103.note: SNMP polling requests go from manager to agent, with responses returning; traps are initiated by agents. Replication alone is not a substitute for independently recoverable backups.

MCSC-104.alt: Training, validation and test sets in a machine-learning workflow

MCSC-104.alt: Comparison of supervised classification and unsupervised clustering

MCSC-105.alt: Breadth-first and depth-first traversal of a five-node graph
MCSC-105.note: For the pictured graph and ascending neighbour order, recursive DFS visits 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5; the displayed DFS order and stack steps are inconsistent.

MCSC-105.alt: Product rule, pigeonhole principle and mathematical induction

Illustrative literature-review matrix comparing fictional papers A, B and C

MCSC-201.alt: IoT architecture from sensors and microcontroller to gateway, network and dashboard

MCSC-201.note: QoS describes MQTT protocol delivery behaviour under its specified conditions; it does not provide unconditional end-to-end delivery, physical accuracy or application-level guarantees.

MCSC-202.alt: Illustrative research protocol from question and ethics through pilot and revision
MCSC-202.note: This is a general example; the need for ethics review or consent depends on the study and institution.

MCSE-202.alt: End-to-end data science workflow with sources of bias
MCSE-202.note: The figure contains minor garbled text. Split data before fitting learned preprocessing, and do not assume that measuring or adjusting for some confounders alone proves causation.

MCSE-202.alt: Numerical example of Simpson’s paradox across two treatment groups

MCSC-301.alt: Research alignment from problem and question to analysis and conclusion
MCSC-301.note: Exploratory work can use prior ideas or hypotheses. Causal inference requires a suitable design and justified assumptions; controlling some measured confounders does not automatically prove causality.

MCSC-301.alt: Hypothesis testing decision matrix with Type I and Type II errors
MCSC-301.note: A p-value concerns results at least as extreme as observed under the null model, not simply the probability of the exact observed data. Actual Type I error can be less than the stated significance level.

MCSC-302.alt: Illustrative dissertation proposal structure from problem to milestones
MCSC-302.note: Some text is repeated. A research gap should be supported by a sufficiently broad review; a few examples cannot prove that no related work exists.
